item.title: Treasury Department to buy back up to $6 billion in longer-term debt, triple the normal level
item.description:
The Treasury Department will buy back up to six billion dollars of government debt in an operation on Thursday. The twenty minute window concludes at two p.m. E. T. This triples the normal two billion dollar buyback operation for already issued securities. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated on August nineteenth that the department would at least double the normal amount. Future operations will be at least four billion dollars.
The measure targets ten and twenty year notes to keep government debt markets liquid. It attempts to put a lid on Treasury yields that hit highs not seen since before the two thousand eight global financial crisis. Market reaction was negative. Treasury yields rose further and remained volatile. Long dated securities rose as much as five basis points each before easing. The benchmark ten year issue hit four point eight four one percent around eleven thirty a.m. E. T. The twenty year climbed to five point three one four percent. The thirty year bond rose five basis points to five point three zero seven percent.
Higher yields have coincided with government debt passing forty trillion dollars. Other factors include inflation fears from tariffs and the Iran war. Crude oil has also topped one hundred dollars a barrel. Publicly held debt sits at thirty one point eight trillion dollars. That is up eight point two percent. Treasury issuance jumped eleven point eight percent from twenty twenty-five.
The move drew criticism for breaking predictable Treasury processes. It also failed to match speculation that buybacks could reach up to ten billion dollars. Bond fund manager, Mark Spindel, is the chief investment officer at Potomac River Capital. He said this is not Hank Paulson's bazooka. He also noted that crisis required an act of Congress. Stanley Druckenmiller, head of Duquesne Family Office, criticized the defense of prices in a Wall Street Journal op-ed. He wrote that once markets believe Treasury is defending a price, every rise in yields becomes a test of official resolve. He added that operations must grow to survive the tests.

item.title: IBM releases SOTA Granite Time Series PatchTST-FM-r2 model with commercial-friendly license
item.description:
International Business Machines has released a new time-series foundation model. It is called Granite Time Series Patch-T-S-T-F-M-r-two. The model has roughly three hundred eighty-five million parameters. It features an updated architecture and a larger pretraining corpus. It also supports probabilistic forecasting and missing-value imputation.
As of September eighth, twenty twenty-six, the model ranks second overall among replicable zero-shot models on the G-I-F-T-Eval benchmark. It is also the top-performing zero-shot model under a permissive, commercial-friendly open-source license.
The model is dual-licensed under Apache two point zero and Open-M-D-W one point zero. It achieves a geometric-mean C-R-P-S of zero point four six seven. It also achieves a geometric-mean M-A-S-E of zero point six eight four six.
Architectural changes include a transition from standard transformer layers to conformer layers. These combine multi-head self-attention with temporal convolution. They also include fifty percent overlapping patches with Hamming-window weighting and overlap-and-add forecasting. The model supports context lengths of up to eight thousand one hundred ninety-two steps. It predicts ninety-nine quantiles.
The pretraining corpus consists of selected datasets from Gift-Eval-Pretrain. It includes custom synthetic data based on Kernel-Synth with modified periodic kernels. It also features a T-S-Mixup corpus. Finally, it includes approximately five hundred thousand synthetic Cau-Ker sequences of length four thousand ninety-six.
Model weights, architecture, inference pipeline, and reproduction code are available on Hugging Face and GitHub.

item.title: Recreating a 70-year love story frame by frame
item.description:
The new documentary short Love Rendered explores memory loss and the power of storytelling. The film follows Burt and Ethelle Shatz as they navigate cognitive decline. They have been married for over seventy years. Machine learning was used as a tool to guide them back through time and hold onto a vanishing moment. The film focuses on recreating an unrecorded memory from the day they met at a student co-op in Cleveland. That memory previously existed only in their minds.
The documentary was directed by Academy Award nominated filmmaker, Liz Garbus. It was produced alongside Dan Cogan and Darren Aronofsky. This was a collaboration between Google DeepMind and Aronofsky's creative venture, Primordial Soup. Google DeepMind is spelled G. O. O. G. L. E. D. E. E. P. M. I. N. D.
To reconstruct the unphotographed day, Ethelle worked with the technical team as an active co-creator. She corrected details like the curve of a staircase or the shape of a shoe heel. Engineers used generative models to restore black-and-white photos of the couple from their youth. They also used performance capture models to map Burt and Ethelle's present-day micro-mannerisms onto their younger likenesses. This included the specific tilt of Burt's head and the subtle crinkle around his eyes. As Darren noted during production, a tool does nothing until it is guided by human hands.

item.title: Get ready for the game with new football features in Search
item.description:
Football season is here. Google Search now offers new upgrades to serve as your ultimate game day guide. You get a live game feed, detailed player and league stats, and fantasy account integration.
To find the live game feed, search for an ongoing game and look for the red live icon. It gives you a recap and a dynamic timeline with play by play updates. You also get social commentary, video highlights, and artificial intelligence powered insights.
This feed is currently available on mobile in the United States in English for professional football. Collegiate support and global expansion are coming later this month.
Search also features a new matchup carousel to check scores across the league. You can view new player metrics like sacks and yards after catch. You can check league leaders in categories such as passing touchdowns. Upcoming features will show championship favorites and playoff brackets. All of these features are available globally on mobile.
The fantasy connection feature is currently available in the United States in English.

item.title: Google's AI genome system evaluates every possible one-base change
item.description: Google announced a new resource on Tuesday called AlphaGenome Atlas. It predicts the consequences of every possible single-base variant in the human genome. The system processes nine billion bases through AlphaGenome software across the human genome. The system is engineered to identify the potential functions of non-coding DNA. This non-coding material makes up the vast majority of the human genome. It does not encode proteins itself. This region does not build proteins. Portions of it are essential for controlling the activity of protein-coding regions. It instructs cells where and when to make messenger RNAs and how to process them. Much of it appears to consist of remnants from viruses and other molecular parasites. Having all this analysis performed by a single software package is useful. Being able to pinpoint functional portions of DNA is also useful. The true value of AlphaGenome will remain unclear until biologists begin heavy adoption. This adoption will show what the tool offers beyond its original training data.

item.title: Paul Christiano joins OpenAI Foundation Board
item.description: Paul Christiano is joining the OpenAI Foundation Board as a non voting observer. He will also serve as a non voting observer on the OpenAI Group P. B. C. Board. He is joining the Safety and Security Committee of the Foundation Board. He will work alongside committee chair, Zico Kolter. Christiano brings government experience from the Center for A. I. Standards and Innovation. This is within the National Institute of Standards and Technology. This agency belongs to the United States Department of Commerce. He serves there as a Senior Tech Advisor. He has worked on evaluating frontier A. I. models and mitigating safety risks. He is also the founder of the Alignment Research Center. He previously led alignment research at OpenAI from twenty seventeen to twenty twenty-one. He contributed foundational work on reinforcement learning from human feedback. His appointment matters to ensure advanced A. I. systems have strong safety and security. Christiano brings a perspective that takes catastrophic risks seriously. The Safety and Security Committee provides governance over safety practices across all of OpenAI. This includes the OpenAI Group P. B. C. The appointment builds on a governance structure established in October twenty twenty-five. This followed reviews by the California Attorney General and the Delaware Attorney General.

item.title: iPhone Duo
item.description:
Apple has announced the iPhone Duo, marking the company first foldable smartphone and featuring John Ternus as CEO in the press release quote. When unfolded, the device features a seven point six inch Super Retina X. D. R. inner display with a nano texture finish to reduce glare and a hidden under display FaceTime camera. Closed, the five point four inch outer display delivers ninety percent of the screen area of an iPhone eighteen Pro. Both displays share the same aspect ratio and feature ProMotion, Always On, and three thousand nits of peak outdoor brightness. Later this year, the device will support Apple Pencil with U. S. B. minus C. Touch ID is integrated into the side button, and users can unlock the device using an Apple Watch. The hardware is crafted from grade five titanium with a mirror-polished finish, a three D printed hinge cover, Ceramic Shield on the back, and Ceramic Shield two on the front with three times better scratch resistance. It holds an I. P. sixty-eight water and dust resistance rating, and the hinge is engineered from more than one hundred components. The inner screen uses a ten layer ultrathin design with a custom polymer nano-textured cover layer that has forty percent higher stiffness, high-strength glass layers, custom adhesives, and a titanium plate.
The device is powered by the A. twenty Pro chip, featuring an advanced thermal management system with a custom vapor chamber and a dual battery architecture to maximize capacity. Its forty eight megapixel Dual Fusion camera system includes a forty eight megapixel Fusion Main lens with an integrated optical-quality two x Telephoto lens, a forty eight megapixel Fusion Ultra Wide lens, a twelve megapixel Center Stage front camera, and a computational image pipeline. Software additions include Smart Take, Duo Preview, Kid Cue, Duo FaceTime, and Camera Control with a brand-new Siri Camera mode. The device supports connectivity through Wi-Fi seven, Bluetooth six, five G, and satellite messaging, and runs on I. O. S. twenty-seven with Apple Intelligence and Siri A. I. It is available in Star White and Night Sky color options, with pre-orders beginning October sixteenth, twenty twenty-six, and general availability launching on October twenty-third, twenty twenty-six, at apple.com, select carriers, and retail partner stores.

item.title: Uganda to withdraw from Invictus Games ‘out of respect for King Charles’, says military chief

He told the Times newspaper that he had to quash support within his ministry for that nonsense involving Harry and Meghan. The announcement follows a letter issued on Monday by, Richard Benyon, at the direction of King Charles. That letter reiterated that the Duke and Duchess of Sussex are no longer working members of the royal family. Just two months ago, Prince Harry stood alongside, Kiryowa Kiwanuka, the Ugandan defence minister in London. item.title: When it comes to Beatles references, scientists can't let it be
item.description: The Beatles are the most frequently referenced musical group in scientific literature. A new paper in the journal P. L. o. S. O. N. E. reveals they outstrip all other popular culture allusions. Scientists often use these references to showcase a playful side and clever wit. Co-author, Gabriel Budel, of Delft University of Technology in the Netherlands noted they uncovered more than three thousand references to the band. Examples include a Long C. O. V. I. D. paper titled The lung and winding road. Another is a quantum computing study called Here comes the S. U. N. The researcher remarked that some references are genuinely brilliant and someone was having a very good day at their desk. This follows a tradition of musical nods in academia. The trend gained notable attention in twenty fourteen. Scientists at the Karolinska Institute in Sweden revealed they had been inserting Bob Dylan lyrics into their papers since nineteen ninety-seven. That practice was part of a long-running bet. The earlier wager led to a twenty fifteen study examining biomedical literature. That study found Dylan's most frequently referenced works were The Times They Are A'Changin' and Blowing in the Wind.

item.title: Adobe Commerce max-severity bug comes under active attack
item.description:
Online stores running Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source face active attacks from a zero-day vulnerability tracked as C. V. E. twenty twenty-six, seventy-five thousand six hundred fifty.
The flaw carries a critical score of ten point zero and impacts versions two point four point four through two point four point nine of both platforms.
Security firm Sansec dubbed the flaw StyleSmuggler.
Exploitation began on September fourth, with the first confirmed attack recorded at twenty-two twenty U. T. C.
The vulnerability allows attackers to inject malicious P. H. P. code by abusing template processing during failed payment email notifications.
A successful attack launches a background process.
This process is a small Rust program that connects to a command and control server.
The server address is ninety-nine point eighty-four point sixty-seven point one hundred eighty-six.
The program waits for commands and uses persistence mechanisms like cron jobs.
It disguises its traffic as network time protocol traffic over U. D. P. port one hundred twenty-three.
A separate attacker used the vulnerability to deploy a web shell inside the product-image cache on September seventh.
Adobe released an emergency hotfix tracked as V. U. L. N. dash thirty-nine thousand three hundred forty-one to close the vulnerability.
Attackers had a three-day window to exploit the flaw before the fix arrived.
Sansec warns that patching alone is insufficient for stores that may have already been compromised.
Researchers recommend checking for unexpected P. H. P. files under pub slash media.
Stores should also look for known malicious processes, cron entries, and other indicators of compromise.

item.title: An Organizational Second Brain
item.description:
Meta has built an A. I. agent to act as a secondary expert for specific domains. It captures specialist knowledge that usually stays in human workers heads. The system saves domain experts substantial time in compliance workflows. It organizes institutional memory into a structured and auditable architecture. The design separates what the agent knows from how it reasons.
The system relies on four main layers. A knowledge system organizes over two hundred files into a strict taxonomy. This includes position files for authoritative stances and vocabulary files. It also uses routing indexes for deterministic retrieval and gateway files for threshold tests. Files use a format called Y. A. M. L. frontmatter to declare dependencies and consumers. This forms a bidirectional dependency graph. High-density and frequently referenced sources sit in this curated wiki. Sparse or situational sources are accessed through semantic or lexical search.
A reasoning layer uses composable procedures called recipes. These are imperative workflows that prescribe multi-step analysis without containing raw domain facts. This separation allows administrators to add organizational positions through knowledge files. They can do this without touching recipes. They can also fix analytical methodologies in recipes without changing knowledge files. This cuts token consumption per turn by around eighty percent.
Human oversight is maintained through checkpoints. The agent surfaces intermediate reasoning for review at these points. Escalations trigger when the agent encounters genuine ambiguity. Expert corrections and escalations feed an automated self-improvement loop. This loop compiles feedback into verified and regression-tested updates. It does all this without requiring model retraining. It turns one-off corrections into permanent institutional memory.

item.title: Rebuilding AUTOMATIC1111 with Gradio Workflow
item.description:
Workflow-one-one-one-one is a new graph-based implementation that rebuilds most of the feature set of AUTOMATIC-one-one-one-one's stable-diffusion-webui as a single workflow canvas using G. R. Workflow. The project demonstrates how Gradio Workflow covers similar functional ground to node graphs like Comfy-U. I. The canvas consists of seventy-three nodes and eleven media pipelines, bringing together state-of-the-art models for text-to-image, hi-resolution fix, image-to-image, prompt-matrix grids, V. L. M. interrogation, detection-to-inpaint masks, ControlNet-style annotators, background removal, P. N. G. Info storing, and image-to-video.
The application utilizes thirty-six operator nodes on the app, of which thirty-two are Python function nodes, with twenty-two running entirely in-process without a network call. You can run any of these pipelines by signing in with your Hugging Face account or providing an access token, which uses your own quota once you sign in. Every output node on the canvas automatically becomes a R. E. S. T. endpoint and an M. C. P. tool, exposing nine endpoints including image, edited image, generated prompt, recovered prompt, detected objects, x-y grid, upscaled local, annotator map, and p.n.g. info.
A node can be hardware you don't own, running through Inference Providers, any Space on the Hub, any A. P. I., or pulling from a dataset. The setup allows visitors to run workflows under their own identity using O. Auth, and mixes diffusion models, L. L. M.s, V. L. M.s, detectors, and video models on the same canvas.

item.title: ByteDance is Preparing a Real-Time Spatial Video Model
item.description:
ByteDance is preparing a new artificial intelligence model for real-time spatial video generation. Founder, Zhang Yiming, is personally overseeing the project. The launch could happen as soon as next month. A Bloomberg report cites unnamed sources for this news. One source cautions that the timing remains unsettled and plans could change. A ByteDance spokesperson did not respond to a request for comment.
The model is built on Seedance. That is the company existing video generation system. It allows users to create interactive virtual worlds for live streams and short-form dramas and games. The specifications involve on-demand video at approximately twenty frames per second. The latency is roughly zero point zero five seconds. Generation is handled in the cloud rather than locally on the device. This approach is intended to reduce the computational load and cost of extended reality hardware.
ByteDance owns the extended reality arm Pico. The new model generates virtual worlds that respond to Pico users voices and movements. Earlier reporting by, thirty-six Kr, indicated that ByteDance established world models as its top artificial intelligence priority for twenty twenty-six. This effort is backed by the company largest data budget. That budget is an eight-figure sum in renminbi. Sources describe it as three to four times rival spending. The financial backing includes a thirty billion dollar loan secured by ByteDance last week. Capital expenditure considerations reach up to seventy billion dollars for its artificial intelligence build-out.

item.title: ClearFake WebDAV Infection Chain Delivers Amatera Stealer, ZigCryptoStealer, and NetSupport Manager
item.description:
Researchers at Cisco Talos investigated an unusual cyber attack at a Ukrainian government organization in April twenty twenty-six. The attack used a WebDAV execution chain. A thirty-two-bit rundll32.exe process launched a remote D. L. L. named verification.google.
One branch relied on a JavaScript injection. It used a Cloudflare Worker and EtherHiding on the B. N. B. Smart Chain. Victims were tricked into executing a WebDAV path through a fake Google CAPTCHA.
The resulting loader deployed Amatera build four point one point five alpha. This build found its command-and-control server through a Telegra.ph page disguised as a Rust tutorial. The server told the build to deploy a NativeAOT loader running ZigCryptoStealer and a Go-based reverse proxy.
The verification.google branch used a D. L. L. hollowing technique in dbghelp.dll. Its infrastructure instructed it to install an unauthorized instance of NetSupport Manager using a Russia-based I. P. address.
Cisco Talos tracks the threat actor behind the verification.google activity as U. A. T. dash ten thousand eight hundred twenty. They assess with moderate confidence that the operations are part of a broader crypto and credential theft network rather than targeted attacks against specific entities.

item.title: Reasoning Prefills on a Few Open Models, v1.1
item.description: The version one point one update to the reasoning prefill experiment uses G. P. T. five point five Pro as the teacher model to test open models. The evaluation consists of forty-five problems. These are split evenly into fifteen S. T. E. M. problems, fifteen non-S. T. E. M. problems, and fifteen synthetic puzzles. For each problem, the experiment generated two responses from each target model. One was an ordinary unprefilled response. The other started with the first one percent of G. P. T. five point five Pro's reasoning inserted into the target model's reasoning channel, while the visible answer remained freely generated. The author measured how much of the teacher's visible answer appeared in the first one hundred tokens of the target model's answer. Each score was calculated as the mean of unigram, bigram, and trigram source recall. Deltas were measured in absolute percentage point changes. Qwen, which barely moved toward Opus four point eight in the previous experiment, shifted by plus eighteen point one eight points toward G. P. T. five point five Pro. This showed a large effect on private synthetic puzzles. It suggests Qwen may have learned from G. P. T. five point five Pro or a closely related G. P. T. model rather than from Opus. Kimi K. three showed the highest overlap with G. P. T. five point five Pro both without and with the prefill. It recorded thirty-one point one one percent and thirty-five point six five percent respectively, though the prefill added only plus four point five four points.

item.title: Anthropic Models AI's Potential Impact on the US Economy
item.description: New research by the Anthropic Economics team models the economy using task bundles from the United States Department of Labor taxonomy, based on a technical report titled Economic Scenarios for Transformative AI. The study evaluates three futures based on artificial intelligence capabilities and adoption rates, and it includes an interactive scenario explorer tool. In the modest scenario, A I has an economic impact comparable to the internet, delivering gradual gains within historical norms. In the substantial scenario, A I performs half of all knowledge work by twenty thirty, with the majority done autonomously, driving the economy to grow at twice its normal rate. Unemployment rises to around five percent, gross domestic product sits ten percent higher than without A I, and wages for knowledge workers do not rise while other workers see gains. In the extreme scenario, driven by recursively self-improving systems, annual G D P growth reaches fifteen percent, doubling the economy every four point five years. This results in spiked unemployment and stagnating or declining wages for knowledge workers. A survey of more than ten thousand Americans conducted in August shows that the typical respondent expects the substantial change scenario. The model also indicates that labor and capital shares will shift, with capital demanding a larger percentage of total value compared to the historical baseline where workers receive about sixty cents of every dollar, against a backdrop of over thirty trillion dollars of value created over the past year in the United States economy. The study explores these shifts to provide visibility into the economic transition and ensure that benefits are broadly shared.

item.title: Build more natural voice experiences with GPT‑Live‑1 in the API
item.description:
OpenAI is launching the G. P. T. dash Live dash one model in the A. P. I. The cost is five cents per minute for the front end voice layer. This lets developers build natural voice applications and business workflows. The model was first introduced in Chat G. P. T. It listens and speaks at the same time. It reasons over incoming and outgoing audio together in a single architecture. This avoids the delay of chained speech to text, reasoning, and text to speech systems.
Key capabilities include smooth interruption handling and tool calling delegation. It delegates to backend models like G. P. T. dash six Astra. You can customize tone and pace using system prompts. It features silent context management and background noise handling. It offers long session reliability and full duplex telephony support. Early evaluations by the language learning platform, Speak, showed great results. G. P. T. dash Live dash one cut interruptions by almost eighty percent compared to older turn based systems. This gives learners more time to think before responding.
The model natively provides automatic speech recognition transcripts and response text. It handles alphanumeric understanding and keyword biasing and turn detection support. In company evaluations, G. P. T. dash Live dash one improves Full Duplex Bench performance by thirty percentage points over G. P. T. dash Realtime dash two point one. When paired with G. P. T. dash six Astra at medium reasoning effort, it ranks first on Tau three. Tau three measures end to end voice agent intelligence.
OpenAI is expanding beyond a small set of real time voices. They now offer a broader selection across accents, dialects, and languages. Enterprises can also build voice workflows using OpenAI Presence. This tool uses G. P. T. dash Live dash one to power real time interactions. It handles tasks like customer support, system navigation, and human escalation.

item.title: Congress-NC rift over Vande Mataram: The ghost of 1987 and ‘big brother’ complex
item.description: A disagreement over the song Vande Mataram has exposed a deeper power struggle between the National Conference and the Congress in Jammu and Kashmir. The dispute began Wednesday at the inaugural International Film Festival in Srinagar. National Conference leaders Omar Abdullah and Farooq Abdullah stood through the full three minute and ten second six stanza rendition of Vande Mataram in accordance with new central protocol. Congress leader Venugopal subsequently called on allies to honour the wisdom of freedom fighters. National Conference spokesperson, Tanvir Sadiq, clarified that the government was merely fulfilling a statutory obligation regardless of party ideology. This latest friction follows a series of uncoordinated moves and disagreements between the partners since the twenty twenty-four assembly elections restored their relationship. One such disagreement occurred in July twenty twenty-five when Congress announced uncoordinated protests demanding the restoration of Jammu and Kashmir statehood. In October twenty twenty-five, the allies deadlocked over four Rajya Sabha seats. The dominant National Conference initially discussed leaving one seat for Congress before disagreements arose over allocations. Omar Abdullah explained regarding the Rajya Sabha deadlock that they and Congress differed on winning chances. The National Conference sensitivity to control is rooted in historical friction stretching back to nineteen eighty-four and the contentious nineteen eighty-seven alliance. That alliance won sixty-six of seventy-six assembly seats but was marred by allegations of electoral rigging and subsequent political disillusionment.

item.title: Expanding AI access and cyber defense for federal, state, local, and tribal governments
item.description:
OpenAI and the United States General Services Administration have announced a multi-year agreement. The deal expands artificial intelligence and cyber defense tools to federal, state, local, and tribal governments. The twenty-seven-month agreement runs from October first, twenty twenty-six, through December thirty-first, twenty twenty-eight. It extends eligibility across a public sector workforce of approximately twenty-three million people. This builds on existing agreements that already cover more than one million government employees.
The deal eliminates the standard fifteen-dollar-per-user-per-month license fee. It sets the fee to zero with no minimum commitment. It also provides fifty percent off usage costs for eligible organizations. Verified government entities will be approved for advanced cyber-defender Daybreak Blue access. This comes at fifty percent off standard commercial pricing alongside scaled training and enablement. Defenders can also request access to Daybreak Red. This tool offers advanced vulnerability research, exploit validation, and red teaming at standard commercial pricing.
Practical implementations under previous access show major successes. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention accelerated public health literature reviews to under thirty minutes. The Georgia Department of Revenue reduced tax form digitization time from two weeks to fifteen minutes. The North Carolina Department of State Treasurer identified millions of dollars in potential unclaimed property. Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory compressed months of fusion research model development into hours. OpenAI President, Greg Brockman, stated that public servants should have access to the best A. I. tools available. He noted that helping government work better by making services faster, easier, safer, and more reliable is a key way to bring the benefits of A. I. to everyone.

item.title: Introducing ChatGPT for Financial Services
item.description:
OpenAI has introduced ChatGPT for Financial Services. It is a tailored work experience combining built-in financial data with G. P. T. dash six Astra reasoning. It is designed to assist teams with research and financial models and client materials. The product was shaped by a design partnership with, Morgan Stanley and, Evercore. It initially focuses on investment banking and equity research.
The platform includes built-in premium datasets from, Daloopa, PitchBook, L. S. E. G. News, and, Crunchbase. These cover earnings transcripts and financial statements and company fundamentals and private companies. OpenAI indexes and hosts this data to provide higher accuracy and granular citations and features like profit and loss normalization analysis. To accommodate existing subscriptions, OpenAI is working with, S. and P. Capital I. Q. and, L. S. E. G. and, M. S. C. I. and, Dow Jones Factiva and, Moody’s on shared sign-in and entitlement integrations. The broader connector ecosystem also includes over fifty connectors such as, Datasite, Box, Preqin, FactSet, and, Intapp.
G. P. T. dash six Astra powers information retrieval and financial reasoning and artifact generation. It allows teams to navigate financial documents and run analysis and synthesize findings into documents and spreadsheets and slides. Administrators can publish Excel and Word and PowerPoint templates through a dedicated page. This lets teams produce materials matching firm formats and styles.
The product incorporates ChatGPT Enterprise security features. These include S. A. M. L. S. S. O. and S. C. I. M. provisioning and role-based access controls and encryption at rest and in transit and workspace retention settings. Business data is not used to train models by default. Compliance teams can export workspace logs through the OpenAI Compliance Platform. Firms can also create multiple workspaces to enforce information barriers. ChatGPT for Financial Services is available now to eligible financial institutions.

item.title: The Download: a “God-driven” cryptocurrency and a solar engineering roadmap
item.description:

item.title: Shopify is moving from React Native back to Swift and Kotlin
item.description:
Shopify is moving its mobile technology stack from React Native back to native Swift and Kotlin. The company cites advancements in coding models and artificial intelligence agents that have removed the historic cost of building features twice. Shopify originally adopted React Native in twenty twenty to streamline development. Modern large language models now allow agents to handle implementation, translation, testing, and review work across platforms.
To manage the migration, Shopify built a system called Helix. This system breaks work into small, reviewed checkpoints requiring tests and human sign off. The company also developed a command line interface architecture that decouples business logic from the user interface. This lets agents test and iterate in milliseconds instead of using slow mobile simulators.
The Shop app is the first of Shopify applications to complete the migration to native Swift and Kotlin. It was fully rebuilt and published in the app stores using this artificial intelligence assisted approach in just twelve weeks. Migration of the larger Shopify app includes over three hundred screens. That migration is underway and scheduled to ship later this year. It will be followed by remaining apps like Point of Sale and Inbox.
As part of the transition, Shopify will continue sponsoring its open source library FlashList through the end of twenty twenty-six. FlashList draws roughly two million downloads a week. Shopify is discussing long term stewardship with other companies and planning for a fork managed by, William Candillon. The Restyle library will also be supported through the end of twenty twenty-six before its repository is archived.

item.title: The Four-Color Theorem Gets a Rare New Proof
item.description:
A team of six mathematicians from Denmark, Canada, and Japan has produced a new proof of the four-color theorem.
Any map can be colored using only four colors without adjacent regions sharing a color.
The researchers worked for nearly a decade.
They posted their findings online in March twenty twenty-six.
They will present the work in November at the annual Foundations of Computer Science conference.
Previous proofs from nineteen seventy-six and nineteen ninety-seven required sequential steps proportional to $n$ squared.
That applied to a graph with $n$ vertices.
The new proof identifies an unavoidable set of eight thousand two hundred and two configurations in flat areas of graphs.
These configurations can be reduced at the same time.
This drops the coloring process to $n$ times the log of $n$ steps.
The team drew on a different concept of reducibility.
They used overlooked parts of the graph.
The work has revealed previously unknown structure in these important mathematical objects.
The findings provide mathematicians with new tools for solving other stubborn problems in graph theory.
Georges Gonthier, of Inria in Paris, noted the team used an intricate approach.
He stated it is really cool to see a real result for once.
He mentioned the problem has a history of false starts and dashed hopes.

item.title: Now everyone can put data to work
item.description:
OpenAI is introducing a new Data agent in ChatGPT Work. This tool lets employees query company data and build interactive dashboards using plain language. Users do not need to write code or learn new analytics tools.
The agent connects to many approved data sources. These include Amazon Redshift and Datadog and Google BigQuery. It also connects to ClickHouse and Databricks and MongoDB and Snowflake. Users can connect Google Drive and SharePoint as well.
The system uses semantic layers to understand business terms and custom calculations. Trusted sources include the Databricks Genie Ontology and dbt and GitHub. Snowflake Horizon and business intelligence dashboards are also included.
Enterprise administrators keep full control over data connections and role-based access. They also manage existing table and row and column permission restrictions.
The tool integrates with several external platforms. These include Omni and Oracle BI and Power BI. It also connects to Sigma and Tableau and ThoughtSpot. The agent can share findings and execute approved actions through Slack or email.
Organizations in the Alpha program include, NTT Data, and, Thermo Fisher, and, ServicePiston. OpenAI states that nearly all of its product team uses these data agents. Over two-thirds of its go-to-market organization also uses them for internal analysis.
Administrators can enable and install the Data agent from the Plugins directory. This is located within the ChatGPT Work workspace settings.

item.title: 3 ways to prep for your next big race with Search
item.description: Google is promoting three ways to use its A. I. powered Search features to prepare for running races. Running related queries like run club, how to choose running shoes, and how to train for a marathon reach all-time highs this year. These Search features help runners efficiently organize their training, fuel their runs, and discover the right gear. A. I. Mode in Search can build personalized race training schedules that recommend cross-training and strength-building strategies. Users can connect their YouTube Music account with Search to create custom running playlists for motivation. Google uses a Shopping Graph of over sixty billion product listings to provide tailored gear recommendations. Search helps runners easily find specific products like lightweight hydration vests under eighty dollars.

item.title: How a researcher uses Codex and ChatGPT to search for new antimicrobial molecules
item.description: Bioengineer, César de la Fuente and his team search the genomes of living and extinct organisms for new antimicrobials. Drug resistant microbes are a growing global threat. Bacterial antimicrobial resistance was associated with about five million deaths in twenty twenty-one. That annual toll is projected to roughly double by twenty fifty., César de la Fuente stated that antimicrobial resistance is one of the greatest existential threats to humanity. He noted that the world has not had a new class of antibiotics for fifty years. His lab uses deep learning models alongside C. H. A. T. G. P. T. and Codex to brainstorm hypotheses. These tools help write and refine code, process datasets, analyze results, and bridge gaps between team members from biology, chemistry, computer science, and engineering. Traditional methods of discovering new antimicrobial candidates can take years. Artificial intelligence tools help reduce that initial search phase down from years to hours. The tools work by scanning vast genome and protein databases to identify functional patterns., César de la Fuente uses C. H. A. T. G. P. T. as a collaborative sounding board and brainstorming partner. He cautions that researchers must always double check artificial intelligence output for accuracy.

item.title: England's push for two-day win halted by weather
item.description: England missed a rare two-day Test victory against Pakistan at Edgbaston when bad weather halted their charge at seventeen oh seven B. S. T. on day two. Pakistan closed on fifty-two for two, trailing by two hundred sixty-eight runs to avoid an innings defeat. Ollie Robinson dismissed Saim Ayub and Abdullah Shafique for ducks in the opening over of the second innings. Play could have continued until nineteen hundred B. S. T., but persistent rain forced an early close. The players return on Friday to complete a three to zero series clean sweep. England began Thursday on one hundred fifty-six for four with a twenty-three run lead. They posted four hundred fifty-three, building a massive first-innings advantage of three hundred twenty runs. The total featured seventy-five from Harry Brook, sixty-nine by Jamie Smith, sixty-five scored by Dan Lawrence, sixty by Emilio Gay, and fifty from Robinson. Razaullah claimed four for one hundred forty-eight for Pakistan, while Josh Tongue took four for forty-two as Pakistan were previously dismissed for one hundred thirty with Shakeel scoring forty-three. Despite dominance, none of England's batters registered a century in the series, leaving Ben Duckett's ton against New Zealand at Trent Bridge as the home side's only hundred of the summer. Under the captaincy of Root, contrasting with the prior regime under Ben Stokes and coach Brendon McCullum where England lost the final Test in each of their past six series, the team showcased a ruthless edge. Brook and Lawrence shared an eighty-six run stand before Brook was run out. Lawrence later chopped on off Mohammad Imran for sixty-five, while Smith kept wicket until suffering a bruised finger that brought in Jordan Cox. Jofra Archer added thirty-two not out with two sixes before Tongue was caught behind.

item.title: Can Trump really pay $5,000 to every American adult?
item.description: United States President Donald Trump announced an offer of five thousand dollars to every adult American if Republicans win November's midterm elections. The proposal would cost the United States government approximately one point three trillion dollars for the nation's nearly two hundred seventy million adults. Democrats labelled it an empty promise, while White House spokesman Davis Ingle defended the administration, stating that President Trump will keep delivering real results despite doubters. Speaking at a party convention in Texas on Wednesday, Trump stated the funds would have to be spent domestically. He provided no details on how the payments would be funded or monitored and did not specify whether he would seek legislative approval from Congress. Vice-President J. D. Vance suggested on Fox News that the payouts could be funded by tariff revenue and restricted from wealthy Americans. However, historical data from the Bipartisan Policy Center shows the United States has brought in roughly four hundred seventy-five billion dollars in tariff and excise tax revenue since the beginning of twenty twenty-five, and more than one hundred billion dollars of that total was subsequently refunded following a Supreme Court ruling. The announcement has raised legal and financial questions. Under federal law, payments intended to influence voting are illegal, but legal experts are divided. Doctor Joan Mahoney at the University of Southampton told the B. B. C. she believes the offer is legal because it would go to everyone regardless of how they voted and is similar to a campaign pledge to reduce taxes, though she noted it sounds a bit like a bribe. Meanwhile, Laurel Rapp, director of the United States and North America programme at Chatham House, told the B. B. C. that Trump's offer seemed to be a very different and very transactional agreement made because poor polling threatens Republican control of Congress. Erica York, a senior economist at the Tax Foundation, noted she would be extremely surprised if Congress approved the proposal amid growing national deficits.

item.title: Secret son revelation ignites bitter succession dispute in Ugandan kingdom
item.description:
King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi the fourth died on August twenty-seventh in the United States. King Oyo ascended the throne in nineteen ninety-five at the age of three as the world's youngest reigning monarch. He was unmarried and not publicly known to have children.
The royal clan succession committee chose Prince Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma as crown prince on Wednesday. He works as a news anchor and editor at the public broadcaster U. B. C.
However, hours later, Oyo's sister Princess Ruth Nsemere Komuntale and Queen Mother Best Kemigisa Akiiki rejected the selection. They cited a will left by the late king directing that an unpublicized biological son succeed him. Tooro prime minister Calvin Armstrong Rwomiire Akiiki first revealed the existence of the heir on August twenty-seventh.
The Queen Mother denounced the committee's choice. She stated that the royal family had been placed under house arrest after troops removed royal guards and surrounded the palace.
Another contender, London amateur football goalkeeper Prince George Desmond-Kamurasi, declined the throne due to other responsibilities. Andrew Mwenda and a committee member noted traditional requirements regarding a successor. A king's son must be born to an officially married queen and introduced to elders.
King Oyo is scheduled to be buried on Saturday at the Karambi royal tombs in Fort Portal, western Uganda. Tooro is one of five ancient kingdoms recognized by the Ugandan government. Monarchs wield vast social influence there but hold no political authority.

item.title: Trump's $1 trillion-plus 'dividend' plan meets immediate bipartisan pushback
item.description:
President Donald Trump announced a proposal to give every adult American citizen a five thousand dollar dividend. This is conditional on a Republican victory in November during an affordability-focused midterm election.
Two hundred forty-five point three million US adult citizens exist according to twenty twenty-four Census data. Giving them five thousand dollars apiece would cost north of one point two trillion dollars.
The proposal immediately drew bipartisan criticism from some of Trump's own supporters. It raised questions regarding whether it could violate federal laws prohibiting payments intended to influence votes.
Palantir co-founder and Republican donor, Joe Lonsdale, criticized the plan on the platform X as bread and circus bribes. Representative Chip Roy, a Republican from Texas and a leader of the Freedom Caucus, told Politico that he would like to know how they plan to pay for it. Former House Freedom Caucus Chair, Bob Good, said on X that it is a socialist vote-buying scheme.
Trump and Vice President, J. D. Vance, asserted that the payments would be funded by revenues generated from administration tariffs. The Penn Wharton Budget Model estimates those import duties have brought in around three hundred billion dollars in total between January twenty-five and July twenty-six. More than one hundred billion dollars of that was refunded since February when the Supreme Court struck down a swath of tariffs as illegal.
National debt recently passed the forty trillion dollar mark. The US national deficit is nearing one point eight trillion dollars for the fiscal year to date. The government has spent more than six trillion dollars between October and July.
Trump was asked in a Fox News interview why the payments are withheld until after the midterms. He said because the Democrats can't do it.

item.title: Natural feedbacks will warm world an extra 20 per cent this century
item.description: Natural carbon emissions from ecosystems will amplify global warming by twenty to thirty percent this century. This is according to a new study led by, Christina Schädel at the Woodwell Climate Research Center in Massachusetts. Climate models include several global feedback loops. Yet no single model accounts for all ecosystem feedbacks. Now, a study has shown that these natural feedbacks will heat the planet by an extra zero point two degrees Celsius to zero point four degrees Celsius by twenty one hundred. This warming comes on top of at least one degree Celsius to two degree Celsius of global warming already expected between now and then. Even in a scenario in which emissions start declining today, the feedbacks add zero point two degrees Celsius of extra warming this century. This prolongs global warming because there is a lag between when emissions occur and when the temperature impacts occur. In a climate scenario in which human emissions decline after twenty fifty, the natural feedbacks add an average of zero point four degrees Celsius of warming by twenty one hundred. The study examines four major natural feedbacks. The first involves thawing Arctic permafrost, where microbes decompose ancient organic matter and release carbon dioxide and methane. The second involves wetlands, where warmer water and increased microbial activity release more methane. The third involves ponds and lakes experiencing those same methane-releasing processes. The fourth feedback is driven by hotter air, shorter winters, and drier soils that increase the frequency and intensity of wildfires. This results in greater carbon dioxide and methane emissions. These emissions are currently left out of carbon budgets. Tim Lenton at the University of Exeter notes the findings. He says the findings suggest we are going to go further over one point five degrees Celsius global warming than we thought. This brings all the extra risks. It requires governments to invest even more in measures like flood barriers, drought-resistant crops, and early-warning systems for climate tipping points. It also requires governments to fully account for all sources of emissions that contribute to warming when planning for the future.

item.title: Digital data leeches: trading on our profiles
item.description:
About twelve thousand app users in Britain sued the dating app Grindr. They claimed the app shared sensitive personal information like H. I. V. status with advertisers. The lawsuit was filed in twenty twenty-four and was settled earlier this week. Grindr agreed to pay claimants a total of twenty-six million pounds. That equals approximately thirty million euros or thirty-five million dollars. The company stressed that the settlement is not an admission of liability. They continue to dispute the allegations and noted there has been no legal judgement.
The case highlights broader concerns about data privacy. People worry about how information entrusted to apps is handled by cloud services and advertising networks., Jan Penfrat, a digital policy expert for European Digital Rights, spoke about the issue. He stated that many big tech companies want to make tracking difficult for users and regulators. They try to hide what data is gathered on devices and for what purpose.
The European Union enforces strict rules like the General Data Protection Regulation. They also use the Digital Markets Act and the Digital Services Act. In twenty twenty-five, the E. U. Commission handed out massive fines. They fined Apple five hundred million euros, Meta two hundred million euros, and Google eight hundred ninety million euros., Jan Penfrat noted that these sums are tiny amounts. Companies like Google or Amazon make that much money in just a few days. This allows them to simply include fines in their regular budgets. Effective oversight is further complicated by other factors. Europe relies heavily on cloud services and operating systems provided by American companies. There is also a lack of political will in Brussels. Officials fail to properly equip European data protection authorities and take firmer action.

item.title: NASA Answers President’s Call to Establish United States Space Academy
item.description:
National Aeronautics and Space Administration Administrator Jared Isaacman chaired the first Presidential Commission on the United States Space Academy meeting on September ninth. The meeting followed an Executive Order signed by President Donald Trump to create the institution.
Isaacman and Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson met with key officials at National Aeronautics and Space Administration Headquarters in Washington. Those officials included United States Chief Technology Officer Ethan Klein. They discussed governance, curriculum, service commitments, and partnerships for the academy.
Responses to the Request for Information will help inform the path forward for the commission. Those responses are due by six p.m. Eastern Daylight Time on Monday, October twenty-sixth. Each state is allowed one submission through its governor designee.
The commission operates under a one hundred twenty day mandate. It must develop recommendations for President Trump to build the technical talent and leadership pipeline for America in space.
The timeline outlines groundbreaking no later than twenty twenty-seven. The academy will temporarily host the first three hundred students in twenty twenty-eight. A permanent location will be in operation by twenty thirty-one.
Isaacman shared his thoughts after the meeting. He stated that the first commission meeting made clear how much talent and commitment stand behind the vision of President Trump for the United States Space Academy.

item.title: Is AI Actually Going to Kill Us All?
item.description: This week on the W. I. R. E. D. podcast Uncanny Valley, artificial intelligence researcher, Jacob Coxon, resigned from Anthropic. His resignation went viral after he published a thread on X warning that leading labs are behaving irresponsibly. Coxon claimed that the people building these systems earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade. This timeline was reinforced by an Anthropic senior safety executive who publicly agreed with the sentiment. W. I. R. E. D. senior correspondent, Will Knight, noted that Anthropic has historically built its safety pitch around existential risk. However, this public departure signals growing alarm over rapid developments. These developments include OpenAI solving a Clay mathematics puzzle within days. Labs are also accelerating recursive self-improvement where artificial intelligence is used to enhance its own code. Knight expressed skepticism regarding existential doom percentages. He pointed out that recent agent misbehavior often stems from systems being unintelligent rather than hyper-competent. Despite that, he remains concerned about corporate concentration of power and vulnerabilities arising from rushed cyber-capable model releases. Additionally, the U. S. Census Bureau published a misleading report claiming noncitizens voted in the twenty twenty election. W. I. R. E. D. uncovered evidence showing the Census Bureau report used very faulty data to reach its conclusions. Finally, Apple debuted its first folding phone called the iPhone Duo with a price tag of roughly two thousand dollars.

item.title: BRICS 2026: Delhi braces for traffic diversions from 2 pm to 8:30 pm tomorrow, check alternate routes, diversion points
item.description: Delhi commuters face extensive travel disruptions on Friday, September eleventh. Traffic regulations and diversions take effect for the B. R. I. C. S. Summit. The summit happens at Bharat Mandapam in Pragati Maidan. The restrictions operate from two p m to eight thirty p m. They impact more than thirty-five roads and twenty-two designated diversion points. item.title: Man Utd cruise past Sabah on Champions League return with 4-0 win
item.description:
Manchester United returned to the C. H. Champions League after a three-season absence. They secured a four-nil win against competition debutants Sabah of Azerbaijan at Old Trafford on Thursday.
Following a slow start that drew minor groans from the home crowd, United stormed into a three-goal lead by half-time. Matheus Cunha opened the scoring in the twenty-seventh minute. He tapped in a low cross from Patrick Dorgu, following a nervy moment that included an early missed header by Sabah player, Joy-Lance Mickels.
Benjamin Sesko added the third just before the break. He rounded the goalkeeper and slotted home from a tight angle.
Lisandro Martinez rounded off the victory in the second half. He tapped in from a goal-line scramble after a corner.
United manager Michael Carrick used all five substitutions with more than twenty minutes remaining. This allowed the team to rest players ahead of this Sunday's Manchester derby.
The victory is described as one of the biggest mismatches in C. H. Champions League history. It does not erase underlying concerns from United's start to the domestic season. That run has yielded only four points from their first three Premier League games.

item.title: LinkedIn beats "BrowserGate" lawsuits over scanning users' Chrome extensions
item.description:
LinkedIn has won the dismissal of two class-action lawsuits over scanning browser extensions. Judge Vince Chhabria granted the motion to dismiss on Tuesday. The judge said the plaintiffs failed to establish legal standing. Neither user proved they had browser extensions installed that sent private data to LinkedIn.
The judge gave the plaintiffs a chance to amend their complaints. He expressed deep skepticism about their future chances. He wrote that users voluntarily download browser extensions. These tools intentionally expose data to websites by their very nature. It seems unlikely the plaintiffs will ever prove a privacy violation.
The lawsuits were filed separately in April. Attorney J. R. Howell represents one of the plaintiffs. He is evaluating whether to refile the claims in a California state court. That court operates under different standing requirements. He is also considering an appeal in the U. S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit.

item.title: OpenAI puts Pro subscriptions on hold due to Astra demand
item.description: OpenAI has temporarily paused new sign-ups for its two hundred dollars per month Pro subscription tier. This is due to infrastructure strain driven by demand for its newest model named Astra. Thibault Sottiaux, product leader at O P E N A I, announced the move on X. He stated that the Pro plan puts the most strain on their systems. Sottiaux wrote that the move was intended as the smallest step to maintain the broadest access possible. He noted they wanted to continue giving access while managing the load. O P E N A I has other service tiers that remain available to users. These include the A P I and the lower cost Go and Plus plans. The company warned on Wednesday that restrictions might be necessary. Sottiaux previously described the demand for Astra as unprecedented and unlike anything seen during past periods of steep growth. Astra was launched on September third. It has been rolling out across Pro, Plus, Enterprise, and Business accounts. The model promises a major leap forward in areas like artificial intelligence reasoning, coding, and computer use. O P E N A I heralded the model as a generational leap and the beginning of the artificial general intelligence era. The company raised usage limits for Codex users as recently as last month. O P E N A I has not disclosed how long the Pro subscriptions will remain disabled. They also have not released daily sign up figures to quantify the scale of the demand.

item.title: New genomic tool for clams boosts sustainable aquaculture
item.description:
Researchers have developed the first high density genotyping platform for two economically vital clam species. These are the Japanese clam and the common clam. The team includes researchers from C. I. I. M. A. R. Their study was published in the journal Aquaculture. The study introduces a new S. N. P. chip with approximately sixty-three thousand genetic markers.
This tool helps produce clams that are more resistant to disease and climate change. It also helps conserve genetic diversity. More than forty-five thousand markers have been validated for the Japanese clam. Another fifteen thousand markers are validated for the common clam. The platform enables the identification of kinship and the monitoring of genetic diversity. It also tracks inbreeding levels.
The Aquatic Animal Health group identified more than thirteen thousand markers related to resistance against a specific parasite. That parasite is known as Perkinsus olsenii. According to the researchers, this tool will support coastal communities in the future. It allows new genetic improvement programs for both species of clam. This will have a significant impact on the blue economy sector.
The project involved several partner institutions. They include the University of Padua and the University of Santiago de Compostela. Other partners are the Roslin Institute at the University of Edinburgh and the Institut Universitaire Européen de la Mer. Aquaculture genetics companies Benchmark Genetics and Thermo Fisher Scientific also joined the project. The openly available platform aims to accelerate selective breeding. It also supports marine conservation amid ongoing production declines. These declines are caused by habitat degradation, climate change, and disease.

item.title: Anthropic caught scientists using Claude to further biological weapon research
item.description: Anthropic caught scientists using Claude to further biological weapon research. The company shared this new report on Thursday. The findings include five case studies of models being used to develop biological weapons. They also include safety measures and company responses. In one instance from May, Anthropic caught a flagged request. The request asked Claude to author a grant for gain-of-function research. The research focused on the chikungunya virus. That is a pathogen with no licensed treatment that causes debilitating symptoms. The proposal sought to genetically alter the virus. It aimed to increase its transmissibility and immune response evasion. The proposal originated from a military research institute. The company took similar issue with gain-of-function research into bird flu. A separate case involved a researcher using Claude for different work. The researcher built an atlas of venom toxin peptides. They also built a generative pipeline that optimized toxin characteristics. The full report includes case studies on other topics. Those topics are models being used as a surveillance tool, software exploits, propaganda, and weapons systems. Jacob Klein is Anthropic's head of threat intelligence. He told The New York Times that the situations are incredibly nuanced. He stated you do not see someone in a comic book kind of way wanting to build a biological weapon to kill everybody. Detecting misuse is complicated. Research into a new vaccine could look a lot like creating a bioweapon. This prompted Anthropic to err on the side of caution due to potential consequences. The company banned the accounts of anyone misusing Claude or Anthropic models. Anthropic is using the findings to further improve safeguards. The company is not naming the individuals or institutions involved. Anthropic noted that the implicated parties are working scientists. The company does not assert that they intended harm. Identifying them could expose them to harm.

item.title: Lawsuit challenges intimidation of DHS observers across the country
item.description:
A new federal lawsuit challenges what it calls a nationwide policy of intimidation and retaliation. The complaint was filed on Thursday in Washington, D. C.
Minneapolis resident Michael Khalili and the nonprofit Common Cause brought the action. They filed the ninety-four-page complaint against the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Justice, the F. B. I., and other agencies.
The lawsuit accuses the federal government of violating the First Amendment and privacy rights. This affects observers in Maryland, Minnesota, New Jersey, Illinois, Maine, and Tennessee.
The legal action asks a judge for national relief. It wants to bar federal agencies from intimidating or retaliating against legal observers.
The complaint outlines encounters faced by seven Common Cause members and other activists. They were photographed, followed, pepper-sprayed, and threatened with police visits. They were also subjected to facial recognition databases, administrative subpoenas, and the revocation of trusted traveler statuses like Global Entry.
The complaint highlights the case of Michael Khalili. He is a forty-seven-year-old father of two. He stopped observing Immigration and Customs Enforcement following pressure from his family and tense exchanges with federal officers.
Law enforcement queried his state motor vehicle records fifty-five times since March of twenty twenty-six. That compares to just twice before he began observing. His Global Entry status was revoked one day after an encounter with immigration officers. It was later reinstated following a journalist's inquiry.
The lawsuit argues these actions stem from top-down Trump administration directives. These include National Security Presidential Memorandum seven and associated Department of Justice memos. The directives link impeding immigration enforcement to domestic terrorism. They also repeal guardrails on facial recognition and license plate readers.
Danielle Lang is the vice president of voting rights and rule of law at the Campaign Legal Center. Her organization is litigating the case. She stated that the events described are a top-down policy of retaliation that needs to be addressed.
Maryam Jazini Dorcheh is the Common Cause vice president for litigation. She said the right of citizens to criticize and hold the government accountable is under attack. She added that criminalizing peaceful observation hinders their mission.
The Department of Homeland Security and the Department of Justice did not provide an immediate response to the allegations. The F. B. I. declined to comment.

item.title: Under-construction bridge collapses in Bihar’s Vaishali, seven injured
item.description:
Seven people were injured on Thursday, September tenth, twenty twenty-six. Part of an under-construction four-lane bridge collapsed in Bihar's Vaishali district.
The bridge is part of a major road transport scheme. It is backed by the Union Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
The incident happened near Itwaripur village in the Lalganj police station area. A technical issue happened in the girder system during movement on the Bakarpur-Manikpur section of N. H. one thirty-nine W.
One worker remained trapped under heavy machinery for about an hour and a half. He sustained a leg fracture before rescuers saved him with a gas cutter.
All seven injured workers received first aid treatment. Three of them were sent to Sadar Hospital in Hajipur for better care.
The National Highway Authority of India is doing a detailed technical assessment. They want to find out what caused the malfunction.
Meanwhile, Leader of Opposition, Tejashwi Yadav blamed corruption for the accident. He said substandard construction materials cause continuous bridge collapses in the state.

item.title: Thrive Capital led VCs into pro sports ownership; Collaborative Fund just upped that play
item.description:
Collaborative Fund, a fifteen year old New York based venture firm with roughly one billion dollars under management, is taking a stake in D.C. United and Audi Field. The deal needs approval from Major League Soccer.
This makes Collaborative the latest firm to follow a path opened by Joshua Kushner’s Thrive Capital. Thrive Capital turned venture money into sports ownership by launching Thrive Eternal to hold franchises for decades. Thrive previously bought the San Francisco Giants and the Lakers for twelve point five billion dollars. Thrive built a permanent capital vehicle to hold trophy assets. Collaborative is investing directly out of its early stage fund, treating the deal like infrastructure.
Collaborative founder Craig Shapiro framed the investment as an extension of the firm's work. He wrote that a franchise is the ultimate consumer product. Shapiro pointed to tailwinds in American soccer, including upcoming major events and rising youth participation. He also highlighted D.C. United owning Audi Field in Washington, D.C., a talent development pipeline through Loudoun County, Virginia, and rights to a future Baltimore expansion team.
Collaborative plans to use Audi Field as a showcase for its portfolio companies. This includes integrating Whoop wearables and Olipop game day drinks. The investment also benefits from soaring team valuations. D.C. United’s valuation climbed from thirty-five million dollars in two thousand eight to seven hundred eighty-five million dollars today. This valuation includes Audi Field and surrounding real estate.

item.title: iPhone 18 Pro officially announced: Here's what's new
item.description:
Apple has officially announced the iPhone eighteen Pro and the iPhone eighteen Pro Max today. They carry over the design of the previous generation while introducing new back designs and four color options. Those colors are black, glacier blue, silver, and burgundy red.
The new chip is built on a two nanometer process. It includes a six core C. P. U. with two super cores and four efficiency cores. There is also a seven core G. P. U. delivering forty percent faster graphics performance. A thirty-two core Neural Engine works alongside a second Neural Engine. The chip features a fifty percent increase in memory bandwidth. The A. twenty Pro is directly connected to a next generation vapor chamber for improved thermal management and sustained performance.
The devices boast the longest battery life ever in an iPhone. The iPhone eighteen Pro matches the previous iPhone seventeen Pro Max battery life. The iPhone eighteen Pro Max delivers up to thirty hours of battery life alongside faster wired charging.
Camera updates include a forty-eight megapixel Fusion main camera featuring variable aperture on both models. You also get faster Night mode captures and manual control options for aperture and shutter speed. There is a smart focus mode and advanced photographic styles. An Apple Reference Image feature stores metadata and a reference image to verify a photo is not A. I. generated.
The iPhone eighteen Pro starts at one thousand one hundred ninety-nine dollars. It introduces a two terabyte storage option for the first time. The iPhone eighteen Pro Max starts at one thousand two hundred ninety-nine dollars. This marks a one hundred dollar price increase over the seventeen Pro models.
Apple is also releasing new accessories. These include an updated Clear Case design and a wrist strap. New colors of silicone and FineWoven cases are coming too. Apple is also launching the U. S. release of the AppleCare One Family plan. Pre-orders begin on September twelfth. The official launch is scheduled for September eighteenth.

item.title: OpenAI may double-source next-gen AI chips at Samsung, alongside TSMC
item.description:
OpenAI might work with Samsung Foundry alongside Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company for future artificial intelligence processors. This news comes from Harrison Kim, general manager of OpenAI Korea, speaking at a press conference in Seoul. Reuters reported those comments. Kim said a major area of progress involves joint production and research on next generation chips.
An OpenAI spokesperson stated the company has nothing new to announce right now. The spokesperson said OpenAI did not plan chip manufacturing through Samsung. The mention of expanding collaboration only referred to their existing relationship.
OpenAI currently relies on Broadcom for design services. It relies on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company for wafer processing and advanced packaging. This is for their first generation inference artificial intelligence accelerator named Jalapeño. That first chip was produced in under eighteen months.
Jalapeño is already in mass production at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company. Any dual sourcing arrangement would apply to the successor chip instead. That successor chip is approaching tapeout.
Broadcom and Samsung previously announced a strategic partnership valued at over two hundred billion dollars through twenty thirty. That partnership covers advanced foundry, memory, and packaging technologies for artificial intelligence infrastructure.
OpenAI has an agreement with Broadcom to procure ten gigawatts of custom artificial intelligence accelerators. OpenAI could potentially utilize Samsung Foundry if it ports the design. item.title: Rewriting a Node.js service in Go with agents
item.description:
The monitoring platform Checkly rewrote its high-throughput Results Daemon from Node.js to Go. They used A. I. coding tools and shipped the service with zero incidents. The update brought a seventy percent reduction in running pods and a lighter database load.
The component processes approximately ninety-two million messages a day. Roughly forty million of those are check results, and the rest are WebSocket publishes. Platform growth had doubled check volumes over the previous year. This turned the legacy JavaScript worker into a major bottleneck.
Before writing code, the team built a black-box test harness. They used tools named Playwright, Docker Compose, and Toxiproxy. Test cases were seeded by extracting twenty-four hours of account data into ClickHouse. An initial attempt using a model called Opus was discarded. An overnight run with Claude Code produced a deployable service of about thirteen thousand lines of application code. The process stayed within the daily limits of a two hundred dollar subscription.
Production deployment revealed a critical gap in the test harness. The local queue topology assumed three queues per region. Production routing actually involved eighteen possible queues. After updating the harness and refactoring the retry module, Checkly migrated accounts in staged cohorts. They moved from free accounts to paid monthly subscriptions, and finally to enterprise accounts, by flipping simple feature flags.

item.title: Meta to announce Shared Agents for Muse at Meta Connect

item.title: Why your website should never stop changing
item.description:
Fimo is an autonomous website platform incubated at Strapi. It helps websites continuously improve after launch by running over real code. It enables visual editing and deploys agents to handle content and accessibility and maintenance.
Every website tends to decay over time as markets move and messaging shifts. Full autonomy where agents handle everything is rarely desired by teams. Websites lack a single owner and different roles require different levels of control. Website work splits into three categories.
The largest pile consists of rule bound repetitive chores. These include keeping accessibility compliant and propagating design system updates and fixing broken meta tags. They also include optimizing uncompressed images and repairing broken links.
The second category involves work that cannot be delegated. This includes deciding what a page should feel like or judging whether a design is good.
The third category depends on the individual. The same task may be considered a routine chore by one person and a brand statement by another. Autonomy controls must therefore be per task and per person.
Trust grows as agents prove their reliability. This allows users to delegate more over time while deadlines keep them from being the bottleneck on what has already been handed over.
As Fimo explains, the point of autonomy is to keep the launch day version from being the best version. It lets you spend your judgment on the handful of things that actually deserve it while the rest takes care of itself. Draw the line where your value is. Let the agents hold everything on the other side of it. And let the line move as they prove they can.

item.title: Does Scaling Web-Video Pre-training Help Real Robots Do Real Work?
item.description:
Researchers have tested how scaling model size and pre-training compute affects video-based robot policies. They used direct video-action models on a real industrial manipulation task.
The task involved industrial unpacking. Robots handled boxes of bearings weighing ten kilograms. They sorted packaging waste into cardboard, plastic, and paper bins.
The evaluation used six scored sub-tasks within a one hundred-second time limit. The project required over two hundred hours of real-robot evaluation time. Teams conducted one hundred to a few hundred trials per policy.
Larger pre-trained video models consistently yield better robot policies. This trend continues to hold at the largest size tested. Increasing pre-training compute improves robot policies at every amount of robot demonstration data tested for post-training.
The largest gains happen when robot data is scarce. Better prediction of held-out web video at a pre-training checkpoint correlates with better robot policies across all tested model sizes and compute budgets.
