item.title: Introducing CUDA Rust for High-Performance GPU Kernel Development
item.description:
In September twenty twenty-six, N. V. I. D. I. A. announced an expansion of its native G. P. U. programming capabilities. The company is maturing C. U. D. A. Rust into twenty twenty-seven and beyond. This bridges the gap for G. P. U. kernels that previously required separate languages.
The initiative offers two distinct tracks for developers. The first option is the S. I. M. T. track. It uses cuda-oxide, a custom rustc codegen backend. This track requires Linux and a G. P. U. with compute capability eight point zero or later. It also requires C. U. D. A. toolkit version twelve point x or newer. Developers need clang with libclang headers and a pinned nightly toolchain. It utilizes specialized types like DisjointSlice to enforce thread safety at compile time. It requires launch contracts to validate configurations against live device limits.
The second option is the Tile track. It is powered by cutile-rs. This track operates at a higher level of abstraction by performing computations on tiles rather than scalars. Its requirements are lighter than the first track. It needs a G. P. U. with compute capability eight point zero or later. It requires C. U. D. A. thirteen point three and stable Rust one point eighty-nine or newer. It also requires Linux. This track utilizes C. U. D. A. Tile I. R. to just-in-time compile kernels. It does not require a custom nightly toolchain or a local L. L. V. M. build.
Both approaches prevent race conditions and memory aliasing errors at compile time. They ensure that tensor inputs are shared while outputs are exclusively owned by a single writer. This addresses the unpredictable concurrency bugs that frequently pass initial testing before failing in production environments.

item.title: The Deathray: A simple way for an untrusted site to freeze a Mac
item.description:
A new vulnerability called deathray lets untrusted websites completely freeze a Mac computer. A user just needs to click a link to trigger it. The issue affects multiple browsers on macOS including Chrome, Firefox, and Safari on September tenth, twenty twenty-six.
Researcher, Auberon López, disclosed the flaw to Apple Security on July twenty-seventh, twenty twenty-six. Apple declined to prioritize a fix. The company stated that hangs and crashes are not security vulnerabilities.
The attack uses WebGPU shaders to run an infinite loop. A compute shader loops infinitely while a vertex shader tries to read from the same data buffer. This creates a massive resource pileup. It overwhelms the macOS WindowServer process and renders the user interface completely unresponsive. The system eventually triggers a kernel panic and restarts through the watchdog timer.
Apple previously fixed a similar exploit using WebGL in twenty twenty-three. That older exploit was called ShadyShader. It received a designation of C. V. E. dash twenty twenty-three dash forty-four-forty-one with a six point five medium score.

item.title: Hong Kong's Tiananmen activists sentenced to up to seven years in prison

On Friday, the court also fined the Hong Kong Alliance one point five million Hong Kong dollars. That equals one hundred ninety-one thousand US dollars, or one hundred forty-two thousand British pounds. Lee's wife, Elizabeth Tang, told Reuters that her husband plans to appeal his sentence. item.title: Meet the under-35s shaping the future of biotech

item.title: Rapidly scaling online storage to serve over 1 billion ChatGPT users
item.description:
OpenAI technical staff Jon Lee, Chaomin Yu, and Ben Ries detailed how their organization adapted an online storage platform named Habitat. They needed to manage rapid growth supporting products like chat G. P. T.
The platform started in mid-twenty twenty-four as a small Python library that interacted with Azure Cosmos D. B.
It has now grown into a distributed system handling more than seventy million requests every second. It operates across almost forty geographic regions for over one billion weekly users. The system serves more than five hundred petabytes of data.
The platform grew more than ten times year-over-year for the last three years. By the middle of twenty twenty-five, the original client-side library approach reached its operational limits. This prompted OpenAI to decouple the storage logic into a standalone service. The goal was to establish a single point of control for deployments, observability, and data security.
The team consciously accepted technical debt by using Python for a high-throughput service despite known performance overhead and network latency penalties. They wanted to unblock product developers and achieve platform stability. They placed a bet that internal coding models like Codex and G. P. T. would eventually simplify a future migration.
Running Habitat as a Python service required active management of tail latencies caused by asyncio event loop scheduling delays. Engineers discovered that periodic J S O N. parsing of feature flag configurations via Statsig contributed to high tail latencies. Uneven load balancing from default connection pooling behaviors also contributed to these high tail latencies and metastable failures.

item.title: Wasps are disappearing this summer, and scientists are worried
item.description: Britain is facing a mysterious shortage of social wasps this summer. Scientists and pest controllers report unusually low numbers across the entire country. This decline follows a strange sequence of weather in twenty twenty-six. Social wasps have special behaviors and body shields to handle heat. Even so, extreme ground temperatures during recent heat waves may have pushed them past their thermal limits. The few surviving wasps look unusually small this summer. This might be caused by a lack of proper nutrition or extreme heat. Experts say this absence is deeply worrying. Wasps play critical roles in ecosystems as pest controllers, pollinators, and decomposers. A research team led by, Sumner, is asking for public help. They want people to share observations and photographs of visiting wasps. You can join the Wasp Picnic Survey twenty twenty-six, titled Ham or Jam, while sharing outdoor meals. item.title: Tiny nanolaser could cut computer energy use in half
item.description: Researchers at the Technical University of Denmark announced on September eleventh, twenty twenty-six, the creation of an ultra-small nanolaser. This device could allow future computer chips to transmit information using light instead of electricity. It could potentially cut computer energy use by half. The breakthrough was published in the scientific journal Science Advances. The study was co-authored by D. T. U. professor, Jesper Mørk, alongside doctors Meng Xiong and Yi Yu from D. T. U. Electro. The light-trapping structure was originally developed by professor Ole Sigmund's group at D. T. U. Construct. The device was built in the D. T. U. Nanolab clean room facility. It pushes beyond conventional size limits by using a nanocavity to trap and concentrate photons and electrons in a microscopic region. This allows the laser to function at room temperature with minimal energy. Thousands of these lasers could eventually be integrated onto a single microchip to make data centers, smartphones, and computers faster and cooler. According to Mørk, the nanolaser opens up the possibility of creating a new generation of components that combine high performance with minimal size. He stated that the technology can reduce energy consumption in information technology. It can also aid in the development of healthcare sensors where extreme light concentration delivers high-resolution images and ultrasensitive biosensors. Much of the internet already relies on light via fiber optic cables. However, internal computer data still moves through electronic circuits, which produces heat and limits speed. The next major challenge is making the nanolaser operate using electrical power rather than an external light beam. Researchers estimate this hurdle could be solved within the next five to ten years.

item.title: Why Do These Fossil Shells Flip Their Spirals Every Few Millennia?
item.description:
For fifty-six million years, tiny marine organisms called planktonic foraminifera have puzzled scientists by suddenly switching their spiral shell-coiling direction globally all at once.
In nineteen fifty-nine, marine geologist David Ericson linked left-coiling shells in the species Neogloboquadrina pachyderma to ice ages and temperature. Later genetic work and global core sampling discredited that temperature hypothesis.
Recently, a team led by University College London micropaleontologist Bridget Wade synthesized five decades of data spanning multiple ocean basins and climate belts. The analysis revealed that several species flipped their coiling directions simultaneously across the Atlantic, Indian, and Pacific oceans.
For example, Globorotalia scitula shifted from mixed to left-handed coiling fifteen million years ago, and then to right-handed ten million years ago. Pulleniatina obliquiloculata coiled almost exclusively to the right for the past eight hundred sixty thousand years, but prior to that experienced rapid, globally synchronized flips every few thousand years.
The new study hypothesizes that these sudden, worldwide shifts are not adaptive responses to climate change, but accidental markers of significant evolutionary events. Researchers suggest that a new genetic variant or cryptic species develops a broad fitness advantage and rapidly spreads across global ocean basins, much like a viral variant, bringing a specific coiling direction to dominance and leaving a permanent record in the seafloor sediment.
The authors wrote that it seems truly puzzling that a species could exist for millions of years coiling one way, and then suddenly reverse, for no apparent reason.
While the flips appear instantaneous in the geological record, scientists note the actual spread likely unfolded over one thousand years or more, accelerated by global ocean circulation. Because other marine organisms lack such distinct fossil markers, these foraminifera shells offer a rare window into how evolutionary traits sweep across the globe.

item.title: AI is both the best and worst thing to ever happen to mathematics
item.description:
OpenAI announced this week that its artificial intelligence agents solved a major mathematical mystery. The problem is two hundred years old and concerns the Navier-Stokes equations, which describe fluid movement.
These equations form one of the Millennium Prize Problems. The problem carries a one-million-dollar reward. Researchers learned of unpublished progress by a pair of mathematicians, prompting OpenAI to deploy thousands of artificial intelligence agents on the problem.
In just eighty-eight hours, the agents reached a conclusion. They determined that the equations do sometimes blow up. This means a part of a fluid moves infinitely fast. The result proves the equations are imperfect rather than indicating real fluids will misbehave.
This breakthrough is among the biggest in decades. However, artificial intelligence proofs differ from human ones. Artificial intelligence tends to produce convoluted arguments that are difficult to follow. They lack the insight traditionally prized by mathematicians.
The logic can still be verified through formalisation. This is a process turning proofs into code checked rigorously by computers. OpenAI has stated it has also made substantial progress on another Millennium Prize Problem.
This development marks a new era. Mathematics may yield more answers than explanations. The transition raises challenges regarding access, usage, and the role of tech companies. Even so, the tool allows mathematicians to make progress faster than before.

item.title: Turkey-monitoring AI forecasts body weight three weeks ahead with 93% accuracy
item.description:
Researchers at Penn State have built an A. I. and camera system. It can forecast individual turkey body weight up to three weeks into the future. The system is accurate about ninety-three percent of the time. The study was published in Frontiers of Animal Science. It addresses the heavy manual labor and animal handling needed for traditional weight monitoring.
Study senior author, Enrico Casella, noted that traditional methods cause economic and animal welfare concerns. Weight information is essential in the poultry industry to maximize the value of each animal. The average weight of a flock determines equipment settings for processing operations.
The study took place at the Penn State Poultry Education and Research Center. Researchers observed thirty male turkeys from day thirty-seven to day one hundred thirty-three of age. An overhead camera captured normal color images and depth images to reveal the three-dimensional shape and size of the birds. The A. I. used a technique called instance segmentation to tell individual turkeys apart from each other and the background. Researchers trained and tested the system by manually weighing the turkeys five times per week. They used a deep learning neural network called ResNet to analyze the image data.
Previous computer vision systems could not forecast body weight over time. This new system predicts future body weight almost as accurately as estimating current weight. Casella stated that farmers would not need to catch and weigh large numbers of birds manually if cameras could estimate weights reliably. This technology could help monitor growth, plan feed strategies, predict market weight readiness, and reduce labor.
The technology is not ready for every commercial farm yet. The experiment involved only thirty turkeys under controlled conditions. Larger studies are needed to test the model across different farms, environments, and much larger populations.

item.title: SpaceXAI data centre may have led to Mississippi air pollution spike
item.description:
Satellite data shows that temporary gas turbines in Mississippi powering a massive data centre have caused a major spike in nitrogen oxide air pollution. The facility is called the Colossus two data centre and it sits in Tennessee. It came online in twenty twenty-five and is the largest operational data centre in the United States. The site has faced controversy and ongoing legal cases over its use of temporary gas turbines that lack catalytic converters to control emissions.
Researchers led by Kevin Gauld at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology used observations from a satellite to assess the impact on local air quality. The study tracked an increase in turbines from twenty-seven in December twenty twenty-five to sixty-nine by August twenty twenty-six. Satellite analysis showed emissions averaged about seven hundred thirty kilograms per hour between February and August twenty twenty-six. Emissions peaked at eleven hundred eighty kilograms per hour in August twenty twenty-six. By comparison, monthly emissions from a nearby gas power plant in Mississippi averaged twenty-one kilograms per hour. Ronald Cohen stated that the site features a huge number of uncontrolled generators without emissions controls. Peter Zoogman at Minerva University noted that the calculated emissions mean each turbine produces roughly the same level of annual emissions as fifty thousand cars.
In July twenty twenty-six, the company promised to remove all sixty-nine temporary turbines by July twenty twenty-seven. They will replace them with forty-one permanent gas turbines permitted by the Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality in March twenty twenty-six. The company also stated that mobile turbines it manufactures in-house will feature pollution-control technology. The rapid rollout of gas power for new data centres risks locking in decades of additional carbon emissions. The company disputed the satellite findings using a court submission from a third-party air-quality expert. That submission claimed local monitoring stations have not observed notable pollution increases and that site emissions meet regulatory requirements.

item.title: Help Refine Data from Space Telescopes with Artifact InSPECtor
item.description: N. A. S. A. has launched a new citizen science project called Artifact Inspector. The project invites volunteers of all ages to help train artificial intelligence tools. These tools will remove errors from space telescope data. Volunteers will examine real data starting in twenty twenty-seven. The data comes from the Euclid telescope and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. Participants will use smartphones, tablets, or computers to examine real data. They will learn how to recognize artifacts caused by cosmic rays and light glinting off telescope housing. They will also spot errors from electronic quirks. These powerful observatories capture light from millions of distant galaxies. The data helps scientists study questions about the expansion of the universe and dark energy. Participants help improve the instructions guiding artificial intelligence models. These models struggle to accurately distinguish invalid pixels from real astronomical objects. A nine-year-old participant, Maeve F., noted after trying the platform that it is really cool people can help teach computers new skills.

item.title: Houthis claim major advance in Yemen and tighten grip on Red Sea shipping lane

International Organization for Migration director general Amy Pope stated that families are being forced to flee for the second or third time with almost nothing left.
Perim Island sits at the narrowest point of the Bab al-Mandab Strait. This is a crucial waterway used by Saudi Arabia to transport oil to Asia. The conflict escalation has contributed to a surge in global oil prices.

item.title: France: About 20 injured in train derailment
item.description:
A train carrying one hundred eighty passengers derailed on Friday evening on the route between the cities of Rouen and Caen in Normandy, in northwest France.
The accident occurred near the town of Cleon at around seven fifty-four p.m. local time, which was seventeen fifty-four U. T. C.
Local authorities reported that at least forty-four people were injured.
One of the injured was evacuated by helicopter in a critical state, according to, Jean-Benoit Albertini, the head of the local authority.
French Transport Minister, Philippe Tabarot, said one hundred forty firefighters were deployed to the scene.
A police spokesperson stated the train derailed after hitting an unidentified object.
The cause of the accident remains under investigation.
French rail network operator, S. N. C. F. Reseau, suspended traffic on the line.
The operator stated that the priority is to care for the passengers and then to restore safe operating conditions.
Local authorities urged the public to avoid the area.

item.title: With eye on poll, BJP to begin ‘drug-free Punjab’ drive amid row over Dalit villager’s death
item.description:
The B. J. P. announced on Friday, September eleventh, twenty twenty-six, that it will launch Nasha Mukt Punjab Yatras. The campaign starts on September eighteenth. It aims to highlight the drug menace in the state with an eye on the twenty twenty-seven assembly poll. State B. J. P. president, Kewal Singh Dhillon, addressed a press conference. He stood alongside party national vice-president, Manpreet Badal, and former state chief, Sunil Jakhar.
The yatras will cover all one hundred seventeen assembly constituencies. The goal is to turn the fight against drugs into a mass movement. The campaign follows a row over the alleged suicide of a dalit villager. The villager was reportedly pressured to apologise for questioning Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema. The minister faced questions regarding the supply of synthetic drugs known as chitta in the state.
Mister Dhillon identified three major challenges confronting Punjab. They are the growing drug menace, deteriorating law and order, and corruption. Dhillon said that the yatras are not merely an anti-drug awareness campaign. He called it an attempt to confront a grave threat. The threat poses danger to Punjabiyat, our culture, values, and the proud identity of the land of the gurus.
He added that the crisis is tearing families apart. It is pushing youth toward violence and imposing a heavy financial burden. This burden forces families into debt or to sell land and assets for treatment. B. J. P. president, Nitin Nabin, will flag off the first yatra on September eighteenth from Pathankot district. Other marches will follow from Fatehgarh Sahib, Fazilka, and Talwandi Sabo.
In March, Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, made a promise. He promised that the B. J. P. would free the state from drugs within two years if given a chance to form the next government.

item.title: US Open tennis 2026 men’s semi-final: Alexander Zverev v Karen Khachanov – live
item.description: Top seed Alexander Zverev leads Karen Khachanov six to three in their third set. This is the men's semi-final at the U. S. Open on Arthur Ashe Stadium. Zverev took the first two sets six to three and seven to six. Flags flew at half-mast around the grounds on the anniversary of the September eleventh attacks. Arthur Ashe was lit up blue from dusk until dawn. Karen Khachanov entered the court first followed by Zverev. Zverev held a six to three career head-to-head advantage over his opponent. Alexander Zverev praised his opponent by stating he is a great guy and he has known him for many years. If Khachanov wins he would become the lowest-ranked player at number fifty to reach the U. S. Open men's final. This would be since the A. T. P. rankings were established in nineteen seventy-three. The other semi-final features Frances Tiafoe playing against Ben Shelton at approximately seven P. M. local time.

item.title: Khosla Ventures is opening a New York office this fall — its first outpost outside Sand Hill Road
item.description:
Keith Rabois confirmed a major expansion during an appearance at a tech event in New York. Khosla Ventures is opening its first office outside of California. The new outpost is located on fourteenth street in New York and should open this fall. The new space will house several investors including, Rabois. He recently relocated to the East Coast. The office features an executive briefing center. This center will host groups of ten to twelve portfolio companies four days a week. They will meet with Fortune Five Hundred companies there. Rabois explained that portfolio companies love the space because they secure pilots and customers. He expects the office to be very vibrant for that reason.
Rabois expressed confidence in New York for finding junior talent straight out of school. He cited portfolio company Ramp as a prime example. However, he noted that recruiting senior technical talent and experienced executives brings structural challenges. Proven senior executives often live in commuter suburbs outside the city. A mandatory five-day in-office culture is difficult to sustain for them. Commute burdens and family housing costs create these hurdles.
This expansion mirrors a broader shift highlighted in a real estate report released last month. The report from C. B. R. E. found that New York has narrowly surpassed the San Francisco Bay Area in total tech talent headcount. This is the first time this has happened in the thirteen years the firm has tracked the data. Khosla now joins other major venture firms like Sequoia Capital and, Andreessen Horowitz in maintaining a localized presence in New York.

item.title: Emerging SARS-CoV-2 sublineage RE.2.2 displays distinct structural features
item.description: Researchers from the Institute of Microbiology of the Chinese Academy of Sciences led by professor, Gao George Fu have studied the properties of a new coronavirus sublineage. This variant is known as B A point three point two point two, or alternatively R E point two point two. Their study was published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. The team used advanced imaging to find that the receptor-binding domain of R E point two point two binds strongly to the human A C E two receptor. A specific reverse mutation called R four nine three Q creates an extra chemical bond. This bond is the main reason for the strong binding. Advanced mapping also revealed up to twenty-six sugar modification sites on the spike protein. One of these sites at position N five two nine is completely new and has not been seen in previous variants. This modification helps lock the spike protein into a closed shape. Lab tests showed that the variant has changed its ability to hide from the immune system. While it avoided many common antibodies, some older broadly neutralizing antibodies regained their power against R E point two point two. These include S two K one four six and L four point six five. Structural images proved that the G four four six D mutation makes it easier for these antibodies to connect.
